items.title: Chuck Findley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 6, 2023
items.q: And I listened to Lee Morgan, I listened to Kenny Dorham, I listened to — after Bobby Hackett this is. But Bobby Hackett was the one that got me playing like lyrical and tunes and stuff like that. And then I listened to Lee Morgan and like I said, and Nat Adderley I listened to as well.

ctx.x: Did you sit next to Jack Sheldon on occasion?

Oh yeah, oh yeah I sure did. I’ve got a couple of stories about that too, I don’t know — well yeah, I could tell you, I could tell you, beautiful. We were at Universal, we had a nine in the morning call and there was a double session and it was a Monday. And we called him “The Creeper.” Jack was The Creeper. And the reason he was called The Creeper was cause he’d creep in and then he’d creep out. And so we’re doing this nine in the morning double session at Universal and the contractor’s name was Bobby Helfer.…

When you heard Conrad Gozzo playing lead you knew it was Conrad Gozzo you know. When you heard Conte Candoli playing a solo, you knew it was Conte Candoli. You heard Pete Candoli you knew it was Pete Candoli. You know it’s just — Plas Johnson, you knew it was Plas Johnson.
